target_stage: Delhi High Court appeal under s. 39 after remand to the Rent Control Tribunal for a finding on reasonably suitable residential accommodation

IK-112400:L123:span1.text: The appellant took on lease, the first floor of the premises in question from the respondent on January 22, 1964 on a monthly rent of Rs. 250.

IK-112400:L124:span2.text: The respondent who was the owner of the entire premises was then occupying the ground floor.

IK-112400:L124:span3.text: that he required the premises bona fide for his occupation as a residence himself and his family members.

IK-112400:L127:span4.text: He also contended that the landlord's requirement for his occupation was not bonafide.

IK-112400:L127:span5.text: He also accepted his plea that the requirement of the landlord for his occupation was not bona fide.

IK-112400:L130:span6.text: It is the view of both the Tribunals that when eviction is asked for within about I I months of the letting, the claim of the landlord cannot be considered to be bonafide.

IK-112400:L139:span7.text: the portion of the premises in the occupation of the landlord was not reaso- nably sufficient for a family consisting of the landlord, his wife, his son, son's wife and their children.

IK-112400:L140:span8.text: the premises in the occupation of the respondent were not reasonably suitable for his residence.
